title: Flying to Morocco from the US: Routes, Hubs, and What to Expect
excerpt: How to get from the US to Morocco: nonstop options, the best connecting hubs, which airport to fly into, and how to keep the fare down.

image_alts.IMAGE_SLOT_1: A wide-body airliner on the tarmac at a sunny airport with a departures board

body:
Morocco is closer than a lot of Americans expect — a single flight from the East Coast, or one easy connection from anywhere else. Getting the route and the arrival airport right makes the whole trip start smoothly. Here's how flying to Morocco from the U.S. actually works.

Can you fly nonstop to Morocco?

Yes, from a couple of East Coast hubs. Royal Air Maroc — Morocco's national carrier and a oneworld member — operates nonstop service from New York (JFK) and Washington-Dulles (IAD) to Casablanca (CMN), a flight of roughly seven hours eastbound. That's the fastest way in if you're near those airports or can position there. Nonstop schedules change seasonally, so confirm current routes when you book.

Connecting flights from everywhere else

From most U.S. cities you'll make one stop. Two paths dominate:

Via Europe

Connect through a European hub — Paris, Madrid, Lisbon, London, or Frankfurt — on a European carrier. This often gives you the widest choice of departure cities and times, and Madrid and Lisbon are quick hops onward to Morocco.

Via Casablanca

Royal Air Maroc funnels many of its U.S. connections through Casablanca, so you can often route your whole trip on one airline and connect onward to Marrakech, Fez, or elsewhere in Morocco from CMN.

Both work well; the European route sometimes wins on price and schedule, while single-airline routing through Casablanca can mean simpler baggage handling.

Which airport should you fly into?

This matters more than people realize, because it shapes your itinerary.

Casablanca (CMN)

The main international gateway and where most nonstops and connections land. It has a train station right at the airport connecting to Casablanca, Rabat, and Marrakech, so it's a practical entry even if Casablanca isn't your destination. Our Casablanca arrival guide walks through your first hour.

Marrakech (RAK)

If Marrakech is your starting point — as it is for most first-timers doing the classic loop — flying straight into RAK saves you the CMN-to-Marrakech leg. Many European connections serve it directly.

Fez (FEZ)

Useful if you're running the loop in reverse or flying out of the north after Fez and Chefchaouen. Flying into one city and out of another (an "open-jaw" ticket) can save a lot of backtracking.

How to keep the fare down

Morocco fares reward a little strategy. Book a couple of months ahead rather than last-minute. Travel in shoulder season (spring or fall) when you're not competing with peak crowds, which also happens to be the best time to visit weather-wise — see our when-to-go guide. Stay flexible on your exact dates and be open to a one-stop routing, which is frequently cheaper than the nonstop. And consider the open-jaw approach: into Marrakech, out of Fez, so you never double back.

Jet lag and timing your arrival

Morocco is four to five hours ahead of the U.S. East Coast (and more from the West), so eastbound jet lag is real but manageable. An overnight flight lands you in Morocco in the afternoon or evening — the ideal pattern, since you can check into your riad, have dinner, and sleep on local time. Try to stay awake until a normal Moroccan bedtime that first night rather than napping, and you'll largely reset by day two. Building a low-key first day into your itinerary (which our routes do — an easy settling-in day in Marrakech) means jet lag doesn't cost you a marquee experience.

Layovers: friend or foe

If you're connecting, the length and location of your layover shapes the day. A tight connection risks a missed flight if the first leg slips; a very long one turns a travel day into a slog. The sweet spot is a comfortable ninety minutes to a few hours. Some travelers deliberately book a longer layover in a European city — Madrid, Lisbon, Paris — and turn it into a bonus stop, either a few hours in the city or an overnight. If you go that route, check whether you need to collect and recheck bags, and leave margin for it.

Baggage and what to expect onboard

Check your specific airline's baggage rules, as they vary, and note that a single-airline itinerary through Casablanca usually means your bags are checked through to your final Moroccan city, while a self-connected two-airline trip may require you to collect and recheck. On the flight itself, the East Coast nonstops are standard wide-body service; the European carriers vary. Pack essentials — medications, a change of clothes, chargers — in your carry-on in case a checked bag is delayed on a connection, which is the most common minor hiccup.

What to expect on arrival

Remember that you can't get Moroccan dirham before you land, so the first order of business after immigration is an airport ATM — they're in the CMN and RAK arrival halls. Having an eSIM active means you can sort a taxi or check your riad's directions before you've even found the cash machine. Entry itself is simple for Americans: no visa, a passport stamp, and you're through — the details are in our visa guide. Once you clear immigration and grab cash, onward transport is easy: at Casablanca the train station is right at the airport, and at Marrakech official taxis and pre-arranged riad pickups wait just outside. If your riad offered an airport transfer, take it for your first arrival — being met by name and walked to your door removes the one genuinely disorienting moment of a first trip, especially if you land tired and after dark. You can always go DIY on later legs once you've found your feet.

Morocco flights FAQ

Is there a nonstop flight from the US to Morocco?

Yes — Royal Air Maroc flies nonstop from New York (JFK) and Washington-Dulles (IAD) to Casablanca. From other cities you'll connect once, usually via Europe or Casablanca.

How long is the flight to Morocco?

The nonstop from the U.S. East Coast to Casablanca is roughly seven hours; connecting itineraries are longer depending on the layover.

Which airport should I fly into for Marrakech?

Fly into Marrakech (RAK) directly if it's your starting point. Otherwise Casablanca (CMN) has a train connection onward.

What's the cheapest way to fly to Morocco?

Book a couple of months ahead, travel in shoulder season, stay flexible on dates, and consider a one-stop routing via Europe, which often beats the nonstop on price.
